name: Pamela Jiménez
description:
Pamela Jiménez is a Mexican tattoo artist whose creative journey began in dance, where she developed a deep connection with movement, expression, and aesthetics. Her passion for the arts led her to study Advertising Illustration, and she later went on to share her knowledge by teaching drawing classes to children, encouraging new generations to keep their creativity alive and not to trade the pencil for a screen.

Over time, she found in tattooing a new form of artistic expression, specializing in Black and Grey. Her work stands out for its elegant compositions, defined contrasts, and careful handling of light, shadow, and texture.

Inspired mainly by the animal world, she seeks to capture the strength, movement, and essence of each species, blending artistic sensitivity, technical precision, and visual harmony.

She is currently based in Mexico City, where she continues to build an artistic identity in which every piece reflects her passion for art, nature, and detail.

name: Carlos Hernández
description:
Based in Mexico City, I create bespoke fine line tattoos guided by proportion, balance, and restraint.

Each piece begins with a personal idea and is developed around the body — considered, singular, and made to endure.

name: Diego Vago
description:
I’m a tattoo artist specializing in black and grey microrealism, with a focus on organic compositions, botanical elements, and animals.

I love creating pieces that feel natural, delicate, and full of character. I enjoy working with fine details, textures, and contrasts, always striving to find a balance between realism and subtlety.

For me, tattooing goes beyond simply creating an image on the skin. It’s also about capturing memories, telling stories, and transforming meaningful moments into pieces that hold special significance. I believe every tattoo can be a way to preserve something that connects us to who we are, what we’ve experienced, or the people we love.

I enjoy being involved in every stage of the creative process, from the initial idea to the final result, making sure each design has its own unique identity.

My goal is to create tattoos that are truly one of a kind, that feel personal to the wearer, and that preserve their essence over time.

name: Shinae Park
description:
I’m Shinae Park. I was born in Korea, but my soul and my heart are deeply Mexican. Mexico is the home where my art blossoms.

I spent a decade working in fashion design. Those years taught me to understand the curves, movement, and harmony of the female body. Today I bring that same sensitivity to the skin, turning it into a canvas where design and intention come together.

I see every tattoo as an amulet: a unique piece of magic, protection, and personal meaning. Through ornaments, mandalas, and botanical compositions in fine line, I seek to adorn and honor each woman’s body, transforming an idea into a symbol of empowerment. It’s not just ink under the skin. It’s a creative ritual between you and me to awaken your inner strength and celebrate your authenticity.

I’m deeply grateful to the Nomad Studio family in Mexico City for opening the door to this wonderful path and allowing me to share this magic with each and every one of you.

name: Rubén Morales
description:
Ruben Morales is a multidisciplinary artist from Mexico City with a background in graphic design, illustration, and animation.

This foundation has shaped his distinctive tattooing style, blending fine line work and microrealism into compositions that incorporate surrealist and urban elements, inspired by artists such as Banksy, Basquiat, and Norman Rockwell.

As co-founder of Nomad Studio, with over 10 years of experience, he has established himself as one of Mexico’s leading figures in tattoo artistry.

Today, his work continues to evolve, maintaining its meticulous attention to detail and a distinctive signature style that is instantly recognizable on the skin.

name: Roberto Fernández
description:
Ever since I was a kid, graphite pencils were my first form of expression: shadows, volume, and contrast. I spent hours and hours drawing, and I always told my mom that someday I'd make a living from drawing… AND LOOK, MOM, I DID IT!

But it wasn't that easy. I did a lot of things before getting here: school, office jobs, part-time work, and the occasional business venture. Without knowing it, all those experiences would end up leading me to a tattoo studio where I got the chance to become an apprentice.

And that's when my mind EXPLODED. This was what I had been searching for! I had found the thing I wanted to do so badly. But easy, it WAS NOT. I taught myself, practicing at night, studying and drawing until sunrise, until the moment came when I had to tell myself: Roberto, if you want to make a living from drawing, you have to burn your boats and go all in on this.

Over time, I discovered that I could bring the technique I'd learned as a kid with graphite pencils into tattooing, exploring Black & Grey and Gray Wash until I found my own visual identity on skin.

Since then, I've had the chance to travel around my country, take part in exhibitions, visit different studios, and learn from great artists. These experiences have helped me grow and, little by little, build my own style. And if I had to go through it all again to be here today, tattooing, WITHOUT A DOUBT, I WOULD DO IT ALL OVER AGAIN.

I feel deep respect, love, and admiration for this craft, because it gave me the chance to make a living from something I've truly loved since I was little: drawing.

Thank you, tattoo, for being my roof and my food.

name: Mario Palomino
description:
My story with art began long before I ever picked up a tattoo machine. In middle school and high school, I found my first form of expression in graffiti. The streets became my first canvases, and among spray cans, colors, and letters, I discovered that art was much more than a hobby: it was a way to communicate what words couldn't always express.

In time, university came along, and with it new responsibilities and paths that led me away from what I loved so much. For eight years, I set art aside. Still, some passions never disappear, even when they fall silent.

It wasn't until I started working independently that I reconnected with my creative side. I rediscovered my love for drawing, design, and the freedom to create. Along the way, life brought me together with a friend who opened the doors to the world of tattooing and taught me my first steps in the craft.

What began as a new curiosity became one of the most important parts of my life. Today, I've been tattooing for nine years. It has been a path of constant learning, experimentation, and artistic growth, in which I've worked to develop my own identity and push my ideas beyond the conventional.

Throughout this journey, I've also found painting and muralism to be other ways of exploring my creativity. Returning to large formats, experimenting with different surfaces, and transforming spaces through color and composition has allowed me to keep alive the connection to street art that marked my beginnings.

Looking back, I understand that those eight years weren't the end of my story with art, but a pause before I found a new way to live it.

Because sometimes the road takes us away from what we love, only to teach us the true value of coming back.

Today, I'm still that young man who found the freedom to express himself on a wall. The difference is that now my canvases are different, my technique has evolved, and my ambitions are bigger. But the essence remains the same: creating out of the need to express something that deserves to exist.

name: Jenn Ferrer
description:
Jenn Ferrer is a tattoo artist based in Mexico City with a background in digital animation. Her interest in photography and cinema has shaped her artistic perspective, influencing her approach to color, light, and visual composition.

With three years of tattooing experience, her work explores the intersection of fine line, color, and surrealism, drawing inspiration from both traditional and digital art.

Through experimentation with textures, transparency, and delicate details, Jenn continues to develop a distinctive visual language, bringing her creative background into each piece she creates.

name: Milo
description:
With six years of experience in the world of tattooing, Milo has built his artistic path on a passion that emerged unexpectedly while he was studying art. What began as a first approach to tattooing soon became a new way to explore his creativity: he discovered in skin a canvas full of possibilities, where each design could come to life through color, shape, and composition.

His work specializes in neo-traditional, traditional, and full-color styles, with a particular fascination for flowers and animals, which often take center stage in his compositions. His artistic approach stands out for its vibrant colors, bold contrasts, and designs full of movement, aiming for each piece to convey strength, energy, and a life of its own.

Beyond the visual result, Milo sees the tattoo experience as a fundamental part of his work. Every project begins with a conversation in which he gets to know his clients' ideas, references, and expectations, then gradually transforms them into custom designs. His creative process seeks a balance between the vision of the person who will wear the piece and his own artistic interpretation, always prioritizing comfort during the session and proper care of the skin.

Throughout his career, he has taken part in tattoo conventions, winning third place at one of them, and has collaborated with artists and peers from a range of styles. These experiences have enriched his vision and his growth as an artist.

He currently lives in Mexico City, where he works as a full-color specialist at Nomad Studio. With his sights set on new horizons, he aims to take his art and projects beyond borders, exploring new opportunities and sharing his vision of tattooing with people from around the world.

name: Erick Sandoval
description:
Zando is a tattoo artist from Mexico City with 6 years of experience. He studied at the Faculty of Arts and Design at UNAM, and his background in photography has influenced the way he observes and creates images.

His work focuses on fine line, blackwork, and microrealism. Through delicate lines, textures, and contrasts, he transforms personal ideas into pieces thoughtfully designed for each body. He believes a tattoo should not only be visually precise but also capture something meaningful about the person wearing it.
